contents.fallback: A bank sets a currency: the names, rates, small change and conversion order of its coins. It takes the name typed in the Bank name field. Left empty, it is named after the renamed item in your main hand (a name tag renamed in an anvil, for instance), otherwise "Bank #N".

Mints are placed from the page of their bank, 2 blocks in front of you. They all strike the coins of the bank, and each one takes back the coins struck by the others. Each mint only offers the trades ticked for it: strike, small change, conversion, buyback, purse, shop licence.

Exchange offices are placed from the page of their bank too. They change the coins of the banks ticked for them for coins of their bank, and back, metal by metal, at the rate set for them: for the coins given, the metal of the coins given back (10 given → 9 back, for instance). Small coins are not changed.

Players open shops with a licence sold by the mints (its price is set for each bank). Used while looking at a chest or barrel, it places a merchant on it and gives a key: the container becomes the stock, and only opens for whoever holds the key. Carrying the key, click the sign above the merchant to add offers: goods in the main hand, price in coins in the off hand.

Coins take the names typed in the coin name fields. Left empty, they are named after a renamed gold, copper or iron nugget, or renamed prismarine crystals, in your inventory (otherwise "Gold Coin", "Copper Coin", "Iron Coin" and "Diamond Coin"). These items are only read, not consumed.

With small change, the mints also change each coin into small coins, as many as the bank strikes coins per ingot (or per diamond), and change them back the same way. Their name follows the small coin name typed in the menu, where %%s stands for the coin name (Small %%s by default).

Conversion: mints offering it exchange coins struck under a former name for current coins, one for one, and change 64 coins of a number into 1 coin of the next number, and back. Each coin has a number (0 = not converted); by default copper 1, iron 2, gold 3, diamond 4, so 64 copper coins = 1 iron coin, 64 iron coins = 1 gold coin, 64 gold coins = 1 diamond coin.

At a crafting table, 9 coins always give back 1 ingot. Mints offering buyback take the coins of their bank back without loss, at its rates: as many coins as the bank strikes per ingot (or per diamond) for 1 ingot (or diamond). With "coins of every bank", they also take back the coins of the other banks, at the rates of each.

Edit bank… on the page of a bank changes its names, rates, small change and conversion order: all its mints follow. Coins struck before a renaming keep their old name: the mints exchange them one for one for coins under the new name. Edit… on the page of a mint changes its name and its trades.

Each mint sells the purse of its bank for 1 leather and 1 string. It works like a bundle, without limit: put coins of its bank in it, take them out, choose which ones. It shows up to 32 coins, keeps the rest in reserve and shows more as you take them out. Anything else is handed back.

Operators open this menu with /function minted_coins:mint/menu, which also lets them open it later with /trigger minted_coins.mint.menu. Creating or editing a bank or a mint runs an operator command: Minecraft asks you to confirm it.
